title: Fanout stream processors for low-latency console metrics ingestion and aggregation
creator: Aisha Gupta
description:
Summary: Build a resilient, low-latency fanout stream processing layer for Console metrics (UI events, API request telemetry, model invocation stats) to power near-real-time dashboards and alerting. This ticket implements the core queue + stream processors, schema contract, exactly-once / idempotent sink strategy, and deployment plan for canary rollout to prod.

Goals: 1) Ingest metrics with end-to-end 99th percentile latency <= 3s from event generation to dashboard availability for high-priority routes. 2) Provide materialized per-tenant and global rollups for cost and latency breakdowns with 1-minute granularity. 3) Keep storage costs bounded by separating hot (recent 48h) aggregates vs cold raw events. 4) Make pipeline observable: lag, processing time, dropped events, schema evolution errors.

Architecture decisions (summary):
- Ingestion: use Kafka as durable append log (existing infra) with topic partitioning by org_id to keep tenant locality.
- Processing: Flink-based stream processors for windowed aggregations and deduplication; lightweight Kafka Streams alternatives evaluated but Flink chosen for stateful window joins and robust checkpointing.
- Schema: Avro with central schema-registry; include event_id and event_ts for dedup and ordering.
- Sinks: hot-path writes into ClickHouse for rollups (low-latency OLAP) and long-term raw events archived to S3 / partitioned Parquet. Idempotent writes established by upsert patterns keyed by (org_id, metric, window_start).
- Backpressure & scaling: processors use Flink autoscaling based on Kafka consumer lag and state size; use RocksDB state backend with incremental checkpoints.
- Failure modes: plan accepts at-least-once processing at ingestion but enforces idempotent sinks and dedup by event_id to approximate exactly-once semantics where necessary.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Flink adds operational complexity compared to stateless processors; mitigated by a small, dedicated streaming infra on Dedicated capacity and runbooks.
- ClickHouse schema churn needs migration strategy; we'll version materialized views and use rolling migrations.
- Aggregation accuracy vs cost: 1-minute tumbling windows chosen as balance between resolution and compute cost; some use-cases may need sub-minute windows (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end pipeline (Kafka -> Flink -> ClickHouse) deployed to staging and ingesting synthetic traffic at target throughput.
2) 99th percentile ingestion-to-visibility latency <= 3s for 95% of synthetic tenants under normal load.
3) Dashboard queries for 1-min rollups return <300ms for recent 48h.
4) Schema-registry rejection and migration test exercises documented and automated.
5) Runbooks for consumer lag, checkpoint restore, and state rescale documented in Confluence.
6) Canary rollout plan approved by PM and SRE with abort criteria defined.
tasks: Design final Flink job topology and state partitioning
Create Avro schemas and register with schema-registry
Provision Kafka topics with partition strategy and retention for hot/archival lanes
Implement Flink processors: dedup, 1-min tumbling aggregates, per-tenant rollups
Implement idempotent sink connector to ClickHouse with upsert semantics
Set up incremental checkpointing to S3 and test restore scenarios
Add monitoring dashboards for consumer lag, processing latency, checkpoint lag
Load-test with synthetic multi-tenant traffic and iterate cluster sizing
Write runbooks and deploy canary to 10% of tenants, verify correctness
Perform security review and ensure Avro schema fixes don't leak PII
comments: 2026-02-20 - Aisha Gupta: Initial ticket created after design sync w/ PM and SRE. Draft architecture picks Flink + ClickHouse. Action: finalize Avro contract and test dedup approach.
2026-02-25 - Marco Reyes: Proof-of-concept processor done in sandbox; dedup by event_id works but increases state size ~25%. Investigating TTL and compaction strategies for RocksDB state.
2026-03-03 - SRE (Hannah Liu): Flagged checkpoint frequency; suggested moving to 30s incremental checkpoints to reduce recovery time. Also requested retention policy for Kafka topics during failover.
2026-03-07 - PM (Omar Patel): Confirmed dashboards that depend on 1-minute rollups. Agreed on canary for 10% orgs, with fallback to batch path if anomalies detected.

2026-03-10 - Review (Design): Danica Park: Reviewed schema and suggested adding an optional 'route_version' field to support future rollout comparisons. Approved with one follow-up to document default value handling.

2026-03-12 - QA (Riley Adams): Load test results uploaded. At 2x expected peak, 99p latency rose to 6s — next steps: increase parallelism and tune RocksDB options. Added follow-up task to autotune memory configs.

2026-03-14 - Marco Reyes: Implemented autoscaling hook for Flink job manager based on consumer lag metric; preparing canary deployment. Posting PR for infra changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4422
notes: Follow-up after canary: evaluate sub-minute requirements and run a cost analysis vs increased shard count. Consider option to expose raw event stream for external consumption via read-replica Kafka topics.
